column3: Exactly joins faithful deeds to forgiveness and honorable provision, the focus's concluding promise.
Affirms the Creator's guidance without materially clarifying moral pairing or exoneration.
God's knowledge of all speech offers a broad basis for judging the words from which people are cleared.
Repeats the focus's promise of forgiveness and honorable provision for faithful good-doers, though it adds little beyond 34:4.
Frames the surah's binding, clarifying ordinances that contain the accusation and exoneration sequence.
Pairs divine forgiveness with punishment generally, without the focus's distinction between persons or speech.
Explicitly sets the impure apart from the good, supplying the focus's central moral differentiation.
Directly condemns accusing chaste believing women, the immediate harm from which the focus clears its recipients.
Forbids choosing the impure over the good in giving, extending the ethical distinction into conduct.
Declares the impure and good unequal even when the former is numerous, a direct interpretive parallel to the focus's contrast.
Continues the warning never to repeat the conduct that produced the slander from which the focus exonerates.
Its good and barren land image gives a consequential contrast between wholesome and corrupted sources, though metaphorically.
Connects authentic believers with forgiveness and honorable provision, but largely repeats the earlier reward formulation.
Supplies the legal sexual-ethics setting whose categories are distinguished from the false charge in the surrounding passage.
Again promises true believers forgiveness and honorable provision, adding little after the earlier exact parallels.
Prohibits exchanging the bad for the good, a concrete ethical instance of preserving the distinction in the focus.
In the same accusation passage, bodily testimony exposes the speakers' deeds and contrasts with the focus's clearing of the accused.
The human question at the earthquake does not clarify the focus's moral or accusatory setting.
Promises forgiveness and great reward to patient good-doers, but lacks the focus's honorable provision and exoneration.
Begins the next privacy ordinance; it shares the surah's social safeguards but not the focus's accusation theme.
Uses wholesome provision for lawful food, only a distant counterpart to the focus's honorable provision.
The Messenger enjoins good and forbids impure things, offering a broad normative frame for the focus's moral contrast.
A personal hope for forgiveness does not explain the focus's clearing from spoken accusations.
Combines witness, refusal of false association, and disavowal, giving a general pattern of separating oneself from a wrongful claim.
Associates wholesome provision with believers, supporting the focus's promise to those distinguished from corrupt speech.
Its reciprocal pairing of sexual conduct gives the closest local parallel to the focus's paired formulation, while retaining its legal setting.
Ibrahim disavows idolatry, a distant analogue to being declared free of what others say.
Links reverent restraint with tested hearts and forgiveness, but does not address the focus's good/bad pairing or slander.
Immediately precedes the focus: divine truth becomes manifest as the local accusation sequence reaches its resolution.
Faith, charity, and divine knowledge do not materially clarify the focus's distinctive contrast.
Condemns fabricating words and attributing them to God, a relevant pattern of corrupt speech against which innocence is distinguished.
Describes distrust and injustice toward divine judgment, only broadly resonant with corrupt moral judgment.
The call for people to assemble adds no clear connection to the focus.
Describes people received by angels as good and admitted to Paradise, supporting the moral status of the good persons in the focus.
A sexual accusation against Yusuf is investigated, rejected, and replaced by a confession of truth, closely paralleling exoneration from a harmful claim.
Night devotion and charitable spending do not clarify the focus's paired moral distinction or clearing.
Condemns saying what one does not do, a limited speech-integrity counterpart to the false words surrounding the focus.
Requires witnesses for sexual accusations and penalizes unsupported accusers, directly establishing the standard behind the focus's exoneration.
Mentions provision from wholesome things in a historical deliverance, without the focus's distinction or accusation context.
Makes each side free of the other's deeds, a general verbal form of dissociation relevant to being cleared from what is said.
Reaffirms the surah's clarifying signs and instruction, but adds little to the specific focus after 24:1.
Calls a letter honorable, sharing only the honor vocabulary without the focus's moral or accusatory sense.
Calls the revelation the word of an honorable messenger, a lexical resonance with honorable provision but not a close bridge.
Refuses blanket self-exoneration and acknowledges the self's pull to evil, a useful counterpoint to the focus's warranted clearing.
Notes speech directed to messengers and divine forgiveness or punishment, but lacks a direct moral-pairing connection.
Answers a fabrication charge with responsibility and disavowal, a parallel to separating an accused person from corrupt speech.
Completes the local law on false accusers with repentance, reform, and forgiveness, extending the focus's merciful conclusion.
A resurrection objection does not clarify the focus.
Calls God's provision better and lasting, only distantly related to the focus's honorable provision.
The light parable concerns divine guidance, not the focus's clearing from speech or moral pairing.
Places disbelievers among the worst of creation, providing a broad contrary category to the focus's good and corrupt persons.
Recognizing revealed truth and weeping at it does not materially explain the focus's exoneration.
Sets the exceptional sworn-testimony procedure for a husband's accusation, a direct procedural counterpart in the same legal sequence.
God's provision for every creature does not clarify honorable provision as the focus's outcome.
Commands disavowal of others' deeds, a concise analogue to being free of what wrongful speakers attribute.
Contrasts layered darkness with divinely given light, offering only a broad image of moral or epistemic separation.
Pairs a good land with a forgiving Lord, but its prosperity setting adds little after the earlier good/bad imagery.
Ibrahim's renunciation of idolatry is a distant form of separation from corrupt association.
Death and resurrection do not bear on the focus.
Merely names the first and last generations without a relevant connection.
Pairs believing men and women across moral traits and promises forgiveness, supporting the focus's inclusive paired description of the good.
The curse invoked if the accuser lies reinforces the grave accountability for the false speech behind the focus.
God's generosity in the command to read does not clarify the focus.
Pairs charitable men and women with an honorable reward, but the reward formula is weaker and redundant here.
Commands respect for the Messenger's call, sharing the surah's discipline of speech but not the focus's issue.
Condemns false doctrinal claims voiced by mouths, a distant instance of corrupt speech.
Shows a perverse preference for unbelievers over believers, only broadly related to distorted moral judgment.
The rain and resurrection image does not materially clarify the focus.
Cosmic creation and divine forgiveness are not a meaningful bridge to the focus.
Commends repelling evil with good, a constructive ethical response that complements the focus's separation of corrupt speech from the good.
Gives the accused wife's sworn denial of a lying charge, a direct local counterpart to clearing someone from accusation.
God hears a woman's complaint and dialogue, generally affirming the accountability of speech without the focus's distinction.
Warns of hearts inclining to deceptive speech, but its immediate setting is broader and indirect.
The later privacy rule protects household boundaries, a distant social-ethics continuation of the surah.
The description of noble, righteous scribes does not materially clarify the focus.
Contrasts hypocrites and idolaters with believing men and women under forgiveness, but adds little beyond earlier moral pairings.
Depicts a deceptive disavowal after inducing disbelief, a contrast to the focus's rightful exoneration.
Tells the Messenger not to be grieved by hostile speech because God hears and knows, a useful support for those harmed by accusations.
The general promise of forgiveness and great reward is redundant and lacks the focus's distinctive provision.
Completes the wife's oath procedure, relevant to local accusation accountability but less informative after 24:6-8.
Wholesome food and righteous action offer only a broad lexical and ethical resonance.
The generic contrast of punishment and reward adds no distinctive help after earlier reward parallels.
The cloud and hail description does not clarify the focus.
Moses's personal repentance and forgiveness do not materially explain the focus.
Mentions spouses and wholesome provision, but its family-provision setting does not explain the focus's moral pairing.
Answers an evil accusation with witness and disavowal, a meaningful parallel to a person being clear of wrongful speech.
General remembrance, piety, and forgiveness do not clarify the focus.
Human dignity and wholesome provision broadly support the honor restored in the focus, without its accusation setting.
Immediately resumes the passage's appeal to divine grace, repentance, and wisdom that underlies the focus's merciful resolution.
Failure to honor an orphan does not clarify the focus.
Punishment of hypocrites supplies only a broad contrast to the good persons in the focus.
The promise of forgiveness and delayed term does not add to the focus's specific outcome.
A hypothetical claim about other gods does not clarify the focus.
Distinguishes idle oaths from what hearts earn, a limited speech-accountability connection.
Critiques unfounded assumptions and concealed thoughts, broadly resonant with wrongful judgment but not the local accusation.
The misleaders' disavowal of followers is a distant and contrary use of separation from others.
Its spousal mutuality and repentance offer only a remote counterpart to the focus's paired terms.
Noble recording angels do not materially clarify the focus.
Protects the Prophet's household from intrusive conduct and names purity of hearts, a contextual social-ethics support for the surrounding honor safeguards.
God's lack of need for provision does not clarify the honorable provision promised in the focus.
Introduces the group who brought the false allegation, establishing the concrete speech from which the focus clears the good.
Commands believing men and women to presume good of one another and name the allegation a manifest slander, directly preparing the focus's exoneration.
Requires four witnesses and identifies unsupported accusers as liars before God, the decisive evidentiary basis for clearing the accused.
Explains that divine grace and mercy prevented severe consequence for participating in the allegation, framing the mercy echoed in the focus.
Condemns passing the allegation mouth to mouth without knowledge and treating a grave matter lightly, directly contrasting corrupt speech with the focus's cleared people.
Requires believers, on hearing the allegation, to refuse speech about it and call it a tremendous slander, the immediate verbal answer to the focus.
Says that God makes the signs clear and knows wisely, completing the local clarification through which innocence and wrongdoing are distinguished.
Warns against loving the spread of indecency among believers, directly identifies the social injury behind the focus's purification from accusation.
Repeats God's grace, mercy, kindness, and compassion in the same slander passage, reinforcing the focus's promise of forgiveness.
Forbids following Satan's steps toward indecency and wrongdoing, extending the local warning against speech that spreads the allegation.
Commands pardon and overlooking after the accusation crisis, joining forgiveness to the restoration of damaged communal honor.
Requires verifying news brought by an unreliable person lest people harm others in ignorance, a general procedural safeguard against the focus's false speech.
Forbids excessive suspicion, spying, and backbiting, directly protects persons from the corrupt social speech opposed by the focus.
Forbids ridicule, defamation, and insulting labels among believers, a close communal ethic supporting the focus's protection of honor.
Names harming believing men and women without cause a manifest slander and sin, closely paralleling the focus's clearing of believers from what is said.
Condemns throwing an accusation onto an innocent person as bearing slander and manifest sin, a direct general counterpart to the local exoneration.
Names the grave slander against Mary, an explicit case of an honorable woman harmed by false accusation.
Records the accusatory charge brought against Mary, furnishing a narrative instance of harmful speech against a righteous woman.
Begins the competing accusation between Yusuf and the official's wife, a narrative setting for testing claims about sexual misconduct.
Introduces a witness-based material test that distinguishes truth from false accusation in Yusuf's case.
The torn shirt's direction confirms the accusation's falsity, concretely showing exoneration by evidence.
The official recognizes the accusation as a woman's scheme, resolving the claim against Yusuf while remaining a partial narrative parallel.
Forbids pursuing what one has no knowledge of and makes hearing, sight, and heart accountable, a broad epistemic rule against circulating unsupported claims.
Commands steadfast justice even toward those one dislikes, supporting fair judgment rather than prejudice in accusations.
Commands believers to uphold justice as witnesses even against themselves or close relatives, a general norm for evaluating and testifying to claims.
Commands just speech, a concise ethical boundary against the corrupt words from which the focus clears its recipients.
Forbids concealing testimony and holds the heart accountable, complementing the focus's distinction through responsible witnessing.
Develops written contracts and witness procedures, a broader evidentiary parallel without the focus's specific honor and slander setting.
Invokes God's curse on liars in a contested claim, a serious counterpart to the oath and truth-accountability themes around the focus.
